acceptance_status: Automated-inventory checkpoint; full functional/native/manual/performance/release parity remains open.
scope: Rust ToolsForm owns shortcut/provider choice projection, default/create/empty copy, selected draft field plans and current captured-key action targets. Native shortcut/URL validation, configuration, context checks and persistence remain authoritative.

build_input_snapshot.gn_delta: No target/dependency change. Rust bridge adds clear_selection for existing SelectState. Explicit native adapters, preference selector allocation/refresh and browser tests changed. Concurrent root network-policy work remains excluded.
build_input_snapshot.method: Frozen UI overlay base a3afc206f742f0a59da6e65d609ddf1df3c7326d plus 16 explicit live UI overrides (including sidebar_metal.h/mm), with committed own installer/stager hooks; concurrent network-policy changes excluded. Twenty-one prototype source hashes are matched to committed, live and staged inputs.

native_service_patch.license: Generated Chromium header and source hook retain the Chromium BSD-style license; project adapter/tool/model changes use Apache-2.0.

contracts: The opt-in shortcut/provider forms no longer format native configuration into C++ label lists or fill fields by indexing those arrays. The native adapter translates Rust-projected keys/labels into the existing scene picker without native combobox model items. Rust receives opaque IDs, native-formatted chords and UTF-16 display/draft metadata, projects keyed labels and returns native-editor field plans. The native configuration vectors remain browser-service data, not the Rust UI selection model. Views keeps its original index/model/field baseline.

Shortcut labels preserve title/em-dash/native formatted chord; provider labels preserve keyword/name/default marker and the add-new row. The add-new row is an explicit valid create draft with empty fields, not an existing entity with an empty ID. Duplicate labels/IDs have separate control keys; malformed empty native IDs fail closed. Raw UTF-16 fields are preserved.

Rust owns active choice, field draft resolution and recording cancellation on shortcut selection. Projection, reset and page changes invalidate old keys; selection changes invalidate previously active drafts. Generation exhaustion disables the projection without key reuse. Native SceneSelect still supplies the existing Rust prefix/menu/input/Metal drawing and native font/event/focus/AX/menu adapters.

Posted shortcut save/disable and provider save/default/delete commands capture the selected key. At admission Rust requires that key to remain current and active. A newer selection cannot lend its fields/target to the older command. Existing timeline captured-key dispatch is retained. Native widget visibility, form/workspace/profile generation and IME guards remain mandatory.

Native SetShortcut/ParseShortcut/ValidShortcut still enforce reserved/system/editing keys, syntax, conflicts and actual IDs; native Upsert/Remove/SetDefaultSearchProvider enforce template/HTTP(S), uniqueness, limits, existing targets and retaining at least one provider. Native registrations, preferences refresh, global/profile scope and persistence remain unchanged. Displayed URL templates are text only; no browser URL objects or navigation authority cross the bridge.

Six Rust cases cover labels/chords/record cancellation, provider create/default/field plans, stale/reset/page/role drafts, raw UTF-16/duplicate and empty IDs, epoch exhaustion and current-choice command admission. A new shared browser case compares every shortcut/provider label and selected field with the native formatter/configuration, including duplicate Unicode names and default marking; existing actual Cocoa prefix, recording/editor/provider and timeline cases remain covered.

A dedicated Metal browser case queues provider deletion then selects another row, requires both providers to survive and verifies a fresh deletion succeeds. It also queues shortcut disable, switches rows, requires both chords to survive and verifies a fresh disable succeeds. Focused and broad gates use the same final source/binary as the full inventory.

No dependency or browser-service policy was added. Remaining form construction/status coordination, service wording, native node/container ownership and full manual/performance/release acceptance remain open. No controlled CPU/GPU/presentation or memory gain is established.

optional_scenarios.status: Not rerun for this presentation checkpoint. The earlier tools-chrome report retains four default-30-trial passes per backend; none is counted as a current-commit pass.

limits: Native titles/frames and modal/scroll/window/event/focus/AX containers, other forms/panels/layouts and remaining form construction/service wording remain open. Native browser validation, authority, stores and operations remain explicit adapters.
Manual IME/candidate-window, VoiceOver, global RTL, typography/scale/pixel fidelity, pointer/trackpad, detach/reattach and GPU recovery acceptance remain open.
No controlled CPU/GPU/drawable-presentation speedup or memory improvement is claimed.
Normal installed applications/profiles were untouched; no release bundle was packaged/signed. Final shipped-binary Apache-2.0/upstream license/notice acceptance remains open.
